newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S HOWARD REFUSES TAX RATE SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S HOWARD REFUSES TAX RATE SPECULATION.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard, campaigning to rewrite the country's tax system, on Thursday refused to speculate on any new tax rates.

"At this stage, I am not going to hypothesise about different options, I am not going start responding even in a general way to particular rates that are put to me, Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"That will derail the whole process of sensible debate," he said.

Howard was asked in separate radio interviews to speculate how far income tax rates could fall under his reforms and whether his planned broad-based indirect tax would be about 10 percent to 15 percent.
On Thursday, Howard announced a full-scale review of the tax system, widely condemned by business and community groups as outdated, complex and unfair.
Key points of the planned reforms will be lower income taxes, a broad-based indirect tax and no increase in the government's total tax take.
"There are almost a limitless number of ways in which you can reform and change the Australian taxation system within the broad parameters that I laid down," Howard said.
Howard said Canberra would consult state and territory governments and community groups before drafting reforms.
"We have a period of what, 14, 15, 18 months before the next election. The Australian public will know well before the next election where we stand," he said.
Any changes must be approved by parliament's upper house, the Senate, where the government needs the support of at least two non-government senators to pass its measures.
